note: _Dominus autem misit ventum magnum in mari_ (Weber/Gryson) – the Lord sent a mighty wind in the sea. The Clementina has the better and no doubt more original, Jeromian reading: (…) in mare (to the sea, accusative). – Caterina Moro: La traduzione di Gerolamo dei profeti minori. _Adamantius_ 13: 102–125, at p. 119.
_clamaverunt viri ad deum suum_ – everyone cried to his god. – This use of _viri_ in the sense of “everyone” is a Hebraism; in classical Latin, one would say: _unusquisque clamavit_. – Kaulen, p. 173
